newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bankruptcy filings at record level -- courts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bankruptcy filings at record level -- courts.

text.p: The number of U.S. bankruptcy petitions reached an all-time high in fiscal 1996, the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts said Monday.
Bankruptcy filings jumped 25.9 percent to a record 1,111,964 in the 12 months ending September 30, compared with 883,457 filed in the same year-earlier period, the office said.
There were 303,309 bankruptcy filings in the fourth quarter, the largest number in a single quarter.
In the 12 months ended September, the Central District of California reported the largest number of filings of any district, with 97,311.

The Northern District of California, the Northern District of Illinois, the District of New Jersey, the Northern District of Georgia and the Middle District of Florida all reported more than 30,000 bankruptcy filings in fiscal 1996, the office said.

Chapter 7 bankruptcies, which allow individuals to keep exempt property while selling remaining property to pay creditors, were up 27.3 percent, with 761,652 filings in the year, compared with 598,250 the previous year.

Chapter 13 filings, which allow creditors to be repaid in installments over three to five years, were up 23.9 percent with 336,615 filings. Chapter 11 filings, which permit businesses to continue operating while developing a plan to pay off creditors, remained stable with 12,554 filings in 1996 and 12,639 in the year before. Chapter 12 filings rose to 1,096 in fiscal 1996 from 883 in fiscal 1995.
Business bankruptcy filings totalled 53,520 while non-business totals reached 1,058,444.
